title: Game Day Plan: Auto-rollback on SLO Breach (Latency/Error + Monitor Outage)
author: Miles Thornton
body:
## Purpose
This game day validates end-to-end behavior of **automatic rollback on latency/error SLO breach** during model version rollouts. The goal is to confirm:
- The rollout controller correctly evaluates SLO monitors (latency + error) using the standardized monitor identity contract.
- Rollback actions are safe, timely, and do not flap.
- On-call workflows (paging, Slack notifications, runbook links, and audit trails) are usable under real pressure.
- The system behaves predictably under **monitoring outages/staleness** ("unknown" verdict) and does not cause cascading rollbacks.

## Scope
**In-scope**
- Canary and A/B rollouts managed by the rollout controller with auto-rollback enabled.
- Latency SLO and error-rate SLO breaches that should trigger rollback.
- Monitor staleness/unavailability and evaluator lag.
- Notifications (Slack + on-call), audit log events, and console visibility.

**Out-of-scope (for this game day)**
- Quality regressions (prompt/output quality gates).
- Auto-remediation beyond rollback (no auto-rollforward).
- Full observability platform outages unrelated to SLO evaluator dependencies.

## Preconditions / Setup
### Environments
- **Primary:** staging (preferred) or internal production cohort (Redwood internal tenants only).
- **Rollout target:** a test route/model pair with enough traffic to satisfy minimum traffic guardrails.

### Feature flags / config
Ensure these are set before starting (names may differ by environment; confirm with Release Engineering):
- Auto-rollback evaluator enabled for target cohort.
- Rollback executor enabled (traffic split revert path).
- Notifications enabled (incident-bot auto-rollback event type).
- Console endpoints enabled for verdict + rollback history.

### Required access
- Rollout controller service logs + traces.
- SLO dashboards for the target route/model/region/tier.
- Ability to initiate a rollout and adjust traffic split.
- Ability to induce controlled latency/errors in the test model version (or via fault injection).

### Safety guardrails
- Use an internal-only tenant and limit regions to a single region unless explicitly expanding.
- Set **rate limits** on rollback executor (per-tenant) as configured for the test.
- Confirm a stable baseline version is available for rollback (known-good).

## Roles and responsibilities
| Role | Primary | Responsibilities |
|---|---|---|
| Game day lead / IC | Miles Thornton | Drives timeline, callouts, go/no-go decisions, ensures notes captured, declares success/failure, owns follow-ups. |
| Control plane (rollout controller) | Benji Okafor | Rollout config, evaluator/executor behavior, debugging, verifying decision traces + idempotency. |
| SRE / On-call representative | Rafael Mendes | Paging expectations, incident workflow validation, runbook correctness, post-rollback validation steps. |
| Observability (monitors + dashboards) | Allison Grant / Sergio Costa | Validates SLO queries/labels, monitor freshness, alert routing, dashboard panels/links. |
| Telemetry pipeline | Nadia Rahman | Validates metric ingest/label normalization, investigates evaluator lag or missing labels. |
| Console backend | Chloe Martin | Validates verdict UI/API, rollback history rendering, manual override/ack flows. |
| Release engineering | Connor O'Brien | Confirms flag state, staged rollout hygiene, rollback plan for feature toggles. |

**RACI note:** Game day lead is the only person who declares scenario completion and transitions to next scenario.

## Communications plan
### Slack channels
- Primary coordination: **#incidents** (simulated) and **#eng-oncall** for workflow validation.
- Engineering backchannel: **#eng-platform**.

### Incident style
- Run this as a **simulated incident** with a dedicated thread.
- Use standard incident cadence:
  1) Declare scenario + hypothesis
  2) Confirm impact signals
  3) Observe auto-rollback behavior
  4) Validate post-rollback health
  5) Record outcome and issues

### Templates
**Kickoff message (copy/paste)**
- "Starting game day: Auto-rollback on SLO breach. Scenario: <SCENARIO>. Target: <route/model/version/region/tier>. Expected behavior: <EXPECTED>. Primary dashboards: <LINKS>."

**Status update (every 10–15 minutes)**
- "Update: <what we see> | Verdict: <healthy/degraded/breached/unknown> | Actions: <rollback pending/executed/blocked> | Next: <next check>."

**Scenario end message**
- "Scenario complete. Result: <pass/fail/partial>. Rollback triggered: <yes/no>. Time to rollback: <X>. Issues: <bullets>."

## Success criteria (global)
We consider the game day successful if all of the following are true across scenarios:
1. **Correctness:** Rollback occurs only when policy conditions are met (window + threshold + minimum traffic + warm-up rules + baseline comparison if configured).
2. **Timeliness:** Rollback executes within the expected operational envelope.
   - Target: decision in <= 5 minutes after sustained breach (depending on monitor resolution and evaluation window).
   - Executor start within <= 60 seconds after decision.
3. **Safety / anti-flapping:** No repeated rollback attempts for the same rollout beyond idempotent behavior; cooldown prevents oscillation.
4. **Observability:** Console shows verdict transitions and rollback history; audit log events are emitted; controller logs include decision trace.
5. **Operational usability:** Notifications include runbook links and enough context to act; on-call steps are clear.
6. **Dependency behavior:** Under monitor outage/staleness, verdict becomes **unknown** and behavior matches configured fail-open/fail-closed policy.

## Metrics to capture during game day
Capture timestamps for each scenario:
- Rollout start time (T0)
- Onset of induced issue (T1)
- First monitor evidence of breach (T2)
- Evaluator verdict change to breached/unknown (T3)
- Rollback action initiated (T4)
- Rollback completed (traffic split reverted) (T5)
- SLOs recover to healthy (T6)

Also capture:
- Evaluator lag (monitor fetch to verdict)
- Monitor fetch errors / staleness detection
- Number of rollback executor calls (should be 1 per rollout, plus benign retries with idempotency)
- Notifications received (Slack + on-call)
- Audit events observed

## Scenario 1: Latency regression during canary
### Goal
Validate auto-rollback triggers when latency SLO breaches during a canary, and that it reverts traffic split to prior stable version.

### Setup
- Rollout type: Canary (e.g., 5% -> 25% -> 50%).
- Ensure minimum traffic requirement will be met at 25% traffic.
- Ensure warm-up period is configured (or explicitly disabled) and noted.

### Fault injection
Induce latency on the canary version only:
- Add artificial delay in the model-serving path (preferred: feature flag in serving runtime for internal test model).
- Alternate: route canary to constrained capacity to raise queueing/TTFT.

### Expected behavior
- Latency SLO monitor indicates breach for the canary slice (or the route/model with canary weight, per monitor contract).
- Evaluator verdict transitions: **healthy -> degraded (optional) -> breached**.
- Rollback executor reverts traffic split to stable version.
- Cooldown engages to prevent immediate re-roll or repeated rollbacks.

### Validation checklist
- [ ] Monitor identity used by controller matches ADR-0147 labels for route/model/region/tier.
- [ ] Decision trace logs show inputs: threshold, window, sample size/min traffic, baseline compare outcome.
- [ ] Rollback action is idempotent (no duplicate traffic-split edits).
- [ ] Slack notification contains: rollout ID, route/model, version, reason (latency), window, threshold, links to dashboards + runbook.
- [ ] Console shows verdict timeline and rollback entry (who/what initiated: "automated").
- [ ] Audit log records: auto-rollback triggered + traffic split revert.

### Pass/Fail
**Pass:** rollback occurs after sustained breach and restores healthy SLOs; no flapping.
**Fail:** rollback does not occur when policy requires it; or occurs without breach / without meeting minimum traffic; or causes cascading issues.

## Scenario 2: 5xx spike / elevated error rate
### Goal
Validate auto-rollback triggers on error-rate SLO breach and that it can distinguish error spikes from low-volume noise.

### Setup
- Rollout type: A/B or canary at a traffic level that satisfies minimum request volume.

### Fault injection
Induce 5xx errors on the canary version:
- Force upstream dependency failure for canary only (e.g., misconfigured auth header / forced exception).
- Alternatively, introduce a controlled failure rate (e.g., 2–5% 5xx) to test threshold sensitivity.

### Expected behavior
- Error-rate SLO breaches over the configured window.
- Evaluator verdict transitions to **breached** and triggers rollback.
- If traffic is insufficient, evaluator should remain **unknown** or **healthy** (depending on policy), and should not rollback.

### Validation checklist
- [ ] Error-rate query reflects correct numerator/denominator and excludes configured error classes if applicable.
- [ ] Minimum traffic guardrail is enforced (verify using request counts in dashboard).
- [ ] Rollback reason is categorized as "error_slo_breach" in internal metrics.
- [ ] Notifications and audit logs correctly reference error SLO vs latency SLO.

### Pass/Fail
**Pass:** rollback occurs when error-rate breach is real and sustained; does not trigger on low traffic.
**Fail:** rollback triggers on low volume noise; or fails to trigger on clear sustained 5xx spike.

## Scenario 3: Monitor outage / staleness / evaluator dependency failure
### Goal
Validate behavior when SLO monitors are unavailable, stale, or query errors occur. Ensure the system produces an explicit **unknown verdict** and follows fail-open/fail-closed configuration.

### Setup
Pick one of the following approaches (prefer least invasive):
1) Block the evaluator’s access to monitor API in staging (simulate network ACL/permission).
2) Introduce query errors (invalid label key, missing label) for the new monitor identity.
3) Stop/slow the monitor pipeline for the target monitor so data becomes stale.

### Fault injection
- Create a condition where the controller cannot fetch fresh SLO data for >= the staleness threshold.

### Expected behavior
- Evaluator verdict becomes **unknown** with a clear reason (e.g., "monitor_fetch_error" or "stale_data").
- No rollback occurs solely due to unknown, unless policy is explicitly fail-closed and configured to rollback/pause.
- Notifications should indicate monitor outage and link to runbook steps for validating monitors.

### Validation checklist
- [ ] Controller surfaces unknown verdict and does not interpret missing data as breach.
- [ ] Internal metrics increment: monitor fetch errors, evaluator lag, unknown verdict count.
- [ ] Console shows unknown verdict state and reason.
- [ ] Rollout progression behavior matches policy: continues, pauses, or blocks as designed.

### Pass/Fail
**Pass:** unknown verdict is explicit, actionable, and safe; system avoids cascading rollbacks.
**Fail:** system rolls back incorrectly on missing data, or silently stops evaluating without visibility.

## Optional scenario (time permitting): Flapping protection / cooldown
### Goal
Validate cooldown prevents repeated rollbacks/rollout oscillation when metrics bounce around thresholds.

### Fault injection
- Alternate between breach and recovery around threshold for a 15–20 minute period.

### Expected behavior
- After rollback, subsequent evaluations do not trigger additional actions until cooldown expires.

## Run-of-show (suggested schedule, 90 minutes)
1. (0–10m) Kickoff, confirm access, verify baseline dashboards.
2. (10–35m) Scenario 1: Latency regression.
3. (35–60m) Scenario 2: 5xx spike.
4. (60–80m) Scenario 3: Monitor outage/staleness.
5. (80–90m) Debrief, assign follow-ups, confirm artifacts saved.

## Artifacts to capture
- Links to relevant dashboards at the time of breach and post-rollback.
- Rollout ID(s), model version(s), traffic splits.
- Controller logs for verdict transitions and executor actions.
- Slack thread permalink.
- Audit log event IDs.

## Follow-up checklist (required)
Within 2 business days:
- [ ] File issues for any observed gaps (policy semantics confusion, false positives, missing labels, unclear notifications).
- [ ] Update runbook with any missing steps discovered.
- [ ] Update dashboards/alerts if links were broken or context was insufficient.
- [ ] Confirm monitor identity coverage and backlog any required label migrations.
- [ ] Confirm console UX changes needed (verdict clarity, rollback reason phrasing, manual override/ack).
- [ ] Review evaluator metrics (unknown verdict rate, fetch error rate, evaluation lag) and set initial SLOs for the evaluator itself.
- [ ] Share a short summary in #eng-oncall and #eng-platform with pass/fail per scenario and top 3 follow-ups.

## Notes / Known risks
- Low traffic routes may never meet minimum traffic in staging; plan a synthetic traffic generator if needed.
- Metric ingestion delay can shift timestamps; use both dashboard evidence and controller decision trace logs.
- If running in an internal production cohort, coordinate closely with SRE and Release Engineering and keep traffic scope narrow.
